findings.mechanism: decode_frame mallocs the output buffer (decoder.c:29). On the checksum-mismatch return (line 42) it returns FRAME_ERR_CHECKSUM without free(buf), and out->pixels is never set, so the caller has no pointer to it. The RLE-failure path frees buf; this path does not.
findings.cause: Missing free(buf) on the CRC-mismatch early return. Every frame with a damaged trailer leaks its whole decoded payload (4-32 KiB), so RSS grows in proportion to the number of corrupt frames.
findings.evidence: Ran valgrind --leak-check=full ./framedec --iterations 2000: 125 rejected frames, 124 blocks (2,240,512 B) definitely lost plus 1 block (25,600 B) indirectly lost, all allocated at decoder.c:29 via main.c:47. With --damage-every 0 valgrind reports 0 errors and no leaks. Leak count matches the number of rejected (checksum) frames.

findings.mechanism: Static 256-entry CRC table, built once lazily.
findings.evidence: Fixed-size static array guarded by table_ready; valgrind shows no growth.
findings.discriminator: Fixed 1 KiB static storage, initialised once; size is independent of frame count.

findings.mechanism: static raw[64KiB] scratch buffer in the synthetic frame source, reused every call.
findings.evidence: Fixed-size static buffer; the no-damage run has 0 leaks.
findings.discriminator: Fixed size, reused on each call, never grows.
